assessments.summary: Ebola cases are peaking in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with sustained high-level transmission, and imported cases are emerging in Kenya and Nigeria.
Dengue cases in the US have surged significantly, with 57 new cases reported weekly this week, up 533% from the previous 8 months.
Measles cases in the US have increased sharply, with 223 new cases reported weekly this week, up 232% from the previous 8 months.
Global flu test positivity has risen to 8.6% this week, up 12% from the previous month, with US hospital admissions also increasing significantly.
West Nile virus cases in the US have spiked dramatically, with 98 new cases reported weekly this week, up 1762% from the previous 8 months.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US have risen steadily, with 280 new cases reported weekly this week, up 79% from the previous 8 months.
Malaria cases in the US have increased moderately, with 38 new cases reported weekly this week, up 59% from the previous 8 months.
Marburg virus disease cases are falling, with Wikipedia readership at the 66th percentile of the past year.
Mpox cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 51/100, showing a 47% increase in weekly cases compared to the previous 8 months but fewer than last year's total.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising with a score of 50/100, indicating a 48% increase in weekly cases compared to the previous 8 months but fewer than last year's total.
US COVID-19 hospital admissions are at baseline with a score of 47/100, showing a 10% increase in weekly hospitalizations compared to the previous month but low Wikipedia readership.
Global RSV test positivity is at baseline with a score of 45/100, showing a 43% increase in test positivity compared to the previous month but fewer than last year's hospitalizations.
Chikungunya cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 44/100, showing a 7% decrease in weekly cases compared to the previous 8 months but more than last year's total.
Avian influenza (bird flu) Wikipedia readership is at the 38th percentile of the past year, indicating moderate public interest but no specific case data provided.
Meningococcal meningitis cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 34/100, showing a 14% increase in weekly cases compared to the previous 8 months but fewer than last year's total.
